summary.text: 难 means “difficult” or “hard.” It is the standardized simplified form of 難, whose traditional graph is analyzed as a bird-name character; its later use for “difficult” is proposed to be a sound-based borrowing, though the bird-name’s pronunciation is unrecovered.

formation.text: The traditional graph 難 is analyzed as a phonosemantic character for a bird name: 隹 contributes the bird category, while an element associated with 堇 supplies a sound cue. A historical account also describes a bird graph written with 鳥 and 堇. These analyses concern 難, not the internal structure of simplified 难.

components.text: In 難, 隹 contributes the bird category in the proposed bird-name analysis. Historical accounts also describe a bird graph written with 鳥; the bird’s identity and pronunciation are unresolved.

sound.text: Modern Mandarin readings are 隹 zhuī and 難 nán. This current pair does not establish a historical sound role for 隹.

components.text: In 難, an element associated with 堇 is analyzed as phonetic. Accounts differ about related early forms, including changes to their lower parts; the element’s early graphic history is disputed.

sound_limitation.text: These reading comparisons do not independently establish that the element in 難 is 堇 or prove its historical phonetic role.

sound.text: Modern Mandarin readings are 堇 jǐn and 難 nán; this current pair does not establish an ancient relationship.
Baxter–Sagart’s Old Chinese entries give 堇 *[g]rə[r] and 難 *nˤar for “difficult.” This comparison does not establish the element’s identity or historical phonetic role.

history.text: Older accounts describe differing structures for 難: some bronze forms combine 黃 and 隹, while a late Warring States example has 隹 and the phonetic element. The available accounts do not give a complete sequence of graphic changes.
A 1935 simplified-character list included 难 as a counterpart of 難; the 1956 scheme standardized 难 as its simplified form. A specific cursive derivation is not established.

uncertainties.text: The bird name is recorded in historical lexicographic accounts, but its earliest surviving occurrence, identity and pronunciation remain unresolved. Interpretations of the related early 堇 form also differ.
The proposed reuse of 難 for “difficult” depends on a possible sound similarity between the bird name and a separate word; the bird-name pronunciation is unrecovered, so the match is unconfirmed.

senses.text: Historical lexicographic accounts record 難 as a bird name; the earliest surviving occurrence is not dated here.

Bronze contexts are reported for 難 meaning “difficult,” including uses glossed as difficult to do and difficult to approach. The inscriptions are not dated here, so priority among early senses is unresolved.
難 is also used as a noun meaning “difficulty”; the evidence gives no first attestation for this use.

developments.text: The proposed account is that a graph used for a bird name was reused to write the separate word “difficult” because the spoken forms were thought similar. The bird-name pronunciation is unrecovered, so this sound match remains unconfirmed.

limitations.text: The dates of the bird-name and difficulty uses are unresolved. 難老 is recorded as a compound glossed “long-lived,” but this does not establish an independent single-character sense or a connection with “difficult.”

overview.text: 难 means “difficult; hard.” It is simplified from 難, whose older graph is recorded for a bird name; reuse for “difficult” is proposed to depend on sound similarity, but the bird-name pronunciation is unrecovered.

components.text: 隹 contributes the bird category in the proposed analysis of the older graph.
堇 is analyzed as a sound component, though its early graphic history is disputed.

relationships.text: 隹 contributes the bird category in the proposed bird-name analysis of 難.
The element in 難 associated with 堇 is analyzed as phonetic. Its early graphic history is contested, and reading comparisons do not establish its identity or historical sound relation.
The 1956 scheme lists 难 as the standardized simplified counterpart of 難.
